title: Inducing Reward-Free Judging Rubrics that Reduce Over-Crediting in Agent Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2608.13564v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Evaluating language-model agents at scale increasingly relies on a second language model as an automatic judge, because the gold signal, an executable environment reward, is expensive, slow, or unavailable at deployment time. Such a judge is a reward-free proxy whose value depends on whether it can be trusted, yet existing judges either hand-write the scoring rubric, as in G-Eval, or fine-tune the judge's weights, and both tend to credit fluent but unsuccessful trajectories as successes. We instead induce the text of an agent-judging rubric from a small set of ground-truth-labeled trajectories, grounding it in true outcomes. We present RubricForge, which evolves a judge rubric by reflective evolution against labeled trajectories to maximize agreement with the environment reward, freezes it, and applies it to held-out trajectories in one model call with no environment access. The optimized artifact is human-readable text, so every verdict

translated_title: 诱导无奖励评判标准以减少智能体评估中的过度评分
translated_abstract: 大规模评估语言模型智能体日益依赖第二个语言模型作为自动评判者，因为黄金信号——可执行的环境奖励——在部署时可能昂贵、缓慢或不可用。这种评判者是一种无奖励代理，其价值取决于其可信度，但现有评判者要么手工编写评分标准（如G-Eval），要么微调评判者的权重，两者都倾向于将流畅但未成功的轨迹视为成功。我们转而从一小部分带真实标签的轨迹中诱导出智能体评判标准的文本，将其扎根于真实结果。我们提出RubricForge，它通过反思性进化针对带标签轨迹演化评判标准，以最大化与环境奖励的一致性，冻结该标准，并在一次模型调用中应用于保留轨迹，无需环境访问。优化后的产物是人类可读的文本，因此每个裁决都是可解释的。
tldr: 本文提出RubricForge，通过从带标签轨迹中反思性进化出可读的评判标准，替代手工或微调方法，减少对流畅但失败轨迹的过度评分，同时保持与真实环境奖励的高度一致。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces RubricForge, which evolves a readable judging rubric from labeled trajectories via reflective evolution, replacing hand-written or fine-tuned approaches to reduce over-crediting of fluent but unsuccessful trajectories while maintaining high agreement with true environment rewards.
